title: Book Two · Chapter 29: The Story at Their Desk
story:
On Monday, Ronan puts his story page beside the shared card.

Jun opens his own copy. The little clean strip is still on the card. One edge is loose, but the notes are clear.

Miss Wu calls the first pair. The children stay at their desk. One reads, then the other tells the next part.

Ronan counts the pairs. Leo and his partner go before them. Their story is short. Leo's voice is quick and clear.

Ronan wants to begin at once. He turns the card towards himself.

Jun puts a finger beside the first box.

“Our people first,” he whispers.

“I know.”

Then Miss Wu calls them. Ronan looks at the other desks. Several children are watching. Mei has her pencil down. Leo leans back in his chair.

“Our story is about a girl, her mum and a woman,” Ronan begins.

He reads the first lines. His voice becomes faster at the soup. He nearly joins the next two sentences together.

Jun's finger stays beside LUNCH.

Ronan takes a breath.

“The girl returns the bowl after lunch.”

He finishes his part and stops. Jun takes the next part. The woman washes the bowl and puts apples in it.

Jun says the girl takes three apples. He stops almost at once.

“One,” he says. “Three are in the bowl. The girl takes one.”

Ronan points at ONE on the card. Jun nods and finishes the story.

Miss Wu lets the class ask two questions. A child by the wall raises a hand.

“Does the bowl belong to the girl?”

“No,” Ronan says. “The woman lends it to her.”

Another child asks about the order.

“Does she wash it at home?”

Ronan looks at Jun. The word she could mean the girl or the woman.

“The girl or the woman?” he asks.

“The woman.”

“Yes. The woman washes it at her own home. The girl returns it first.”

Jun touches the right lines on his copy. Miss Wu looks at the page too.

“Thank you. Now the next pair.”

Ronan sits back. There is no score beside their names. Miss Wu is already listening to another story. He wants to ask about their place, but that pair is speaking.

Jun rolls his pencil between his hands.

“I said three,” he whispers.

“You changed it.”

“I saw your note.”

Ronan looks at the small ONE. Jun wanted it there on Thursday. The note helped Jun today.

At the end of the lesson, Miss Wu takes the shared cards. They will stay with the class pages for now. Ronan and Jun may take their story copies home.

Jun smooths the little strip once. Then he hands the card over.

At break, Leo asks to see the apple picture. The boys go to Miss Wu's desk.

“May we look at our card?” Ronan asks.

“Yes. Look here,” she says.

Ronan points at the tiny head in the first box.

“That one is a person.”

“It still looks hungry,” Leo says.

Jun draws a mouth on a scrap, far from the class card. Leo adds a big apple. Ronan puts a little leaf on top.

They take the silly picture outside. Mei comes past with her own book page. She shows it to a friend, then walks with her towards the shade. The boys choose a dry place for their ball.

Jun wants a little circle. Leo wants long throws across the yard. They try the circle first. Ronan sends the ball to Jun. Jun throws it high, and Leo catches it against his chest.

“Now a long one,” Leo says.

Ronan moves back. The ball drops short of him. He runs to pick it up, then moves a little closer for the next throw.
studyGuide:
## 重点表达

- belong to＝属于
- leans back＝向后靠
- whispers＝小声说
- smooths＝抚平

## 理解问题

1. Ronan怎样把“She”所指的人问清楚？
2. Jun为什么及时把“三颗苹果”改成“一颗”？

## 从认词到读句子

正文原句：*The woman lends it to her.*

**The woman / lends it / to her.**

那个女人／把它借出／借给女孩。it指碗，her指女孩。
